title_en: How I invest in credit through the AI boom| Bruce Richards
title_zh: 如何在AI热潮中投资信贷｜Bruce Richards
subtitle_zh: Marathon Asset Management联合创始人、CEO兼董事长Bruce Richards谈信贷周期、软件估值重置与私募信贷的真相
description: How I invest in credit through the AI boom| Bruce Richards

turns.en: Welcome to Without Boundaries, a podcast by Russell Investments. Today, we've got the distinct pleasure of Bruce Richards joining us, who's the co-founder, the CEO and the chairman of Marathon Asset Management, so thank you so much for being with us. John, great to be here. Thank you. Thank you. We were really lucky.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Without Boundaries，这是一档由 Russell Investments 制作的播客。今天我们非常荣幸地请到了 Bruce Richards，他是 Marathon Asset Management 的联合创始人、首席执行官（CEO）兼董事长，非常感谢您来到节目。Jon，很高兴来到这里，谢谢。谢谢，谢谢。我们真的很幸运。

turns.en: We were looking at your bio ahead of this, and you've known our research team for a long time. So before we talk about credit, before we talk about markets, you have what you describe as some side hustles. You play chess. You also play tennis. And so one, why do you love playing those so much, and which one teaches you more about
turns.zh: 我们在节目前看了您的履历，您和我们的研究团队相识已经很久了。所以在聊信贷、聊市场之前，先说说您自己形容的那些“副业”：您下国际象棋，也打网球。那么第一个问题：您为什么这么热爱这两项运动？其中哪一个更能让您领悟到关于——

turns.en: investing? Well, chess, as you know, you always want to think a step or two steps ahead on a chess board. And so it quite often just gires your mind towards how you think about investing from that perspective. Sitting across the table from somebody reminds me of, although you're not talking when
turns.zh: ——投资的东西？嗯，国际象棋嘛，你知道，在棋盘上你总要想在前面一步、两步。所以它常常会引导你的思维，让你从那个角度去思考投资。和对手隔着棋盘对坐，会让我联想到——尽管下棋的时候你并不开口说话——

turns.en: you're playing the game, but chess, necessarily, is like negotiating, because negotiating your moves, and you're looking at the opposing player, exactly what their response is. And so I love that aspect. And of course, there's a winner and there's a loser. And so you really do know the score at the end. Tennis, well, I love for the sport.
turns.zh: ——但下棋其实在某种意义上就像谈判，因为你在为自己的每一步棋“谈判”，你盯着对手，看他们究竟会怎么回应。所以我很喜欢这一面。而且当然，棋局有赢家有输家，到最后你是真真切切知道比分的。至于网球嘛，我就是单纯热爱这项运动。

turns.en: And sport, while I wouldn't say, makes you a better investor, and I wouldn't make that claim, I think there are some super interesting aspects of playing a game of singles, where you're strategizing how you're going to play that point, and how that player responds on their next point, much like chess in that regard.
turns.zh: 运动这件事，我不会说它能让你成为更好的投资人，我不下这种断言。但我觉得打单打有一些特别有意思的地方：你会去谋划这一分要怎么打，以及对手在下一分会怎么回应，这一点上和国际象棋很像。

turns.en: And again, there's a winner and a loser, but I just love the sport, because I took it up later in life, tennis, as it did chess, and I'm getting better at both. And so I love that aspect as well. Let's talk about marathon asset management, and in particular, so you've been investing
turns.zh: 同样，这里也有赢家和输家，但我就是热爱这项运动，因为我是年纪稍长之后才开始打网球的，就像下棋一样，而且这两样我都在越做越好，所以我也很喜欢这一点。那我们来聊聊 Marathon Asset Management 吧，尤其是——您从事投资

turns.en: for well over three decades in global credit markets, and it pretty much every asset category. The Russell Investments clients mainly have allocations to you through your emerging market debt portfolios or your multi-asset credit portfolios. Over those years, what is it that you've learned, I guess, that has influenced the current
turns.zh: ——已经三十多年了，而且几乎覆盖每一个资产类别。Russell Investments 的客户主要是通过您的新兴市场债券（emerging market debt）组合，或者您的多资产信贷（multi-asset credit）组合来配置到您这里。我想问，这么多年下来，您学到的哪些东西影响了如今

turns.en: investment philosophy, your investment approach at marathon? It's been a long time, and there's a lot of economic cycles, a lot of financial cycles, that define some of these periods of time, whether it was the Asian currency crisis, or the recession following the dot-com bubble, of course, the biggest double mall in terms of
turns.zh: ——您在 Marathon 的投资理念、投资方法？这确实是很长一段时间了，期间有很多经济周期、很多金融周期定义了一些时段：无论是亚洲货币危机，还是互联网泡沫（dot-com bubble）之后的经济衰退，当然还有信贷周期里幅度最大的一次回撤（drawdown）——

turns.en: credit cycle, the GFC, or more recently COVID. All these different cycles informs, because you think about risk management rule number one is, how will your portfolio perform in the downside? The second aspect is there's been an enormous evolution of the global credit markets during
turns.zh: ——全球金融危机（GFC），或者更近的新冠疫情（COVID）。所有这些不同的周期都在提供借鉴，因为你想想，风险管理的第一条原则就是：你的组合在下行时会表现如何？第二点是，在这段时间里，全球信贷市场经历了巨大的演变——

turns.en: this period of time, and the evolution has taken the credit markets both on the public side and the private side to a stratosphere that wasn't even envisioned when I started at marathon, and I started marathon back in 1998. When you look back over the last 28 years, this has been 2026, and you think about the
turns.zh: ——这种演变把信贷市场，无论是公开市场还是私募市场，都推向了一个平流层般的高度，是我当初创办 Marathon 时根本想不到的——我是 1998 年创办 Marathon 的。回望过去这 28 年，如今已经是 2026 年了，你再想想

turns.en: evolution of the credit markets, both the public and the private credit markets, and all the cycles in between, it's rather remarkable. But what is coming next is transformative and the biggest part of credit development that we will ever see. And I'm talking about AI and the data center build out, and all that power that's needed,
turns.zh: ——信贷市场的演变，无论是公开还是私募信贷市场，以及其间所有的周期，都相当了不起。但接下来要发生的才是真正具有变革性的，是我们将会见到的信贷发展中最大的一部分。我说的就是人工智能（AI）和数据中心的建设，以及所需的全部电力、

turns.en: all the infrastructure that's needed, the infrastructure build out, the re-industrialization of developed nations, as you bring supply chains back, is absolutely stunning and remarkable. We're talking about not a few hundred billion, and not just a couple trillion, but multiple
turns.zh: ——所需的全部基础设施、基础设施的建设，以及随着你把供应链迁回而发生的发达国家再工业化（re-industrialization），这一切绝对是惊人而了不起的。我们说的不是几千亿，也不只是几万亿，而是好几

turns.en: trillions of capital that's needed for this entire development as productivity gains require these cat-bex needs. So I've heard you talk about this a little bit before, so if you don't mind, let's tease out of that a little bit. It is kind of a truly, I guess, historic moment for capital raising that you've described.
turns.zh: ——好几万亿美元的资本，整个这一发展都需要，因为生产率的提升带来了这些资本开支（capex）需求。我之前听您谈到过一点这个话题，所以如果您不介意，咱们把它再展开说说。您描述的，可以说是一个真正意义上的历史性融资时刻。

turns.en: So I was wondering if you could talk about how that might be playing its way out in the opportunities you're finding in your portfolios at the moment. What is the investment opportunity? Investment opportunities is quite broad, and so there are the public markets, and a lot
turns.zh: 所以我想知道，您能不能谈谈这一点当下是如何在您组合里发现的机会中逐步展开的。投资机会是什么？投资机会其实相当宽泛，既有公开市场，而且很多

turns.en: of this credit is coming into the public markets, whether it's high-yield bonds or brothers that they get loans, whether it's in the developed markets or the developing markets, whether it's coming through structured credit being in the CNBS market or the ABS market, or
turns.zh: ——这类信贷正在进入公开市场，无论是高收益债券（high-yield bonds）还是广泛银团贷款（broadly syndicated loans），无论是在发达市场还是发展中市场，无论是通过结构化信贷（structured credit）进入 CMBS 市场还是 ABS 市场，抑或是

turns.en: the other parts of structured market, which forms the CLO market and all the truncers there and the RMBS market. So we see continued growth in structured finance, which is a $4 trillion market today, when we talk about liquid public structure finance, high-yield bonds, loans, US and Europe, nearly
turns.zh: ——结构化市场的其他部分，也就是 CLO 市场及其中的各个分层（tranche），还有 RMBS 市场。所以我们看到结构化金融（structured finance）在持续增长，如今这是一个 4 万亿美元的市场；当我们谈流动性公开结构化金融——高收益债券、贷款，美国和欧洲——将近

turns.en: four trillion, and emerging market debt, both the developing countries and the more developed countries within the emerging markets, which is also a $4 trillion market. So you talk about a $12 trillion tam that's growing in a faster rate than GDP. And then you talk about the private credit markets, which is growing substantially faster
turns.zh: ——将近四万亿美元，还有新兴市场债券，既包括新兴市场里的发展中国家，也包括其中较发达的国家，这同样是一个 4 万亿美元的市场。所以你算下来是一个 12 万亿美元的潜在市场总规模（TAM），而且增速快于 GDP。然后你再看看私募信贷（private credit）市场，它的增长速度要快得多——

turns.en: than the economy or substantially faster than the public credit markets, because we believe those growth rates are in the teens, if not 20% when you look out over the next five to seven years, based upon all the capital needs. And so Marathon is at the crux of all of this in the public credit markets and the private
turns.zh: ——快过整体经济，也快过公开信贷市场，因为我们相信，基于所有这些资本需求，展望未来五到七年，其增速会在十几个百分点，甚至达到 20%。所以 Marathon 正处在这一切的核心，既在公开信贷市场，也在私募

turns.en: credit markets, and it's cross-despectrum. It's not one sector, it's every sector that is fueling the economy, that we're helping finance, that we're investing in. Of course, it's credit selection, and it's going to be enormous dispersion between winners
turns.zh: ——信贷市场，而且是横跨整个谱系的。不是某一个行业，而是每一个在推动经济、我们在帮助融资、我们在投资的行业。当然，关键在于信用甄选（credit selection），而在赢家

turns.en: and losers in individual credits, as well as the individual managers that select those credits. We see a real bifurcation of the mean versus the underperformers versus those that outperform. And those that outperform versus the mean, that was a rather tight spread in years past.
turns.zh: ——和输家之间，无论是单个信用标的，还是甄选这些标的的单个管理人，都将出现巨大的分化。我们看到均值、表现不佳者与表现优异者之间出现了真正的分叉（bifurcation）。而在过去几年里，表现优异者与均值之间的利差其实相当窄。

turns.en: But in this next credit cycle, I'm not talking about an economic cycle, because I think there's economic growth that's going to propel us forward, but there's a credit cycle. The credit cycle has all these underlying sub-sectors that inform who's going to perform well versus those that won't.
turns.zh: 但在下一个信贷周期里——我说的不是经济周期，因为我认为会有经济增长推动我们向前——而是信贷周期。这个信贷周期底下有各种各样的子行业，它们决定了谁会表现好、谁不会。

turns.en: As you think about the multi-asset platform, you talked about different segments of the market that we're more and less attractive right now, I was wondering if you could sort of dive just a little bit deeper on what are some of the areas that you're overweighting
turns.zh: 谈到多资产平台，您提到市场不同板块当下的吸引力有高有低。我想知道，您能不能再深入一点谈谈：目前您正在超配（overweight）的是哪些领域，

turns.en: right now and what are some of the areas that you're underweighting in that multi-asset credit strategy right now. So just more broadly speaking, thinking about the K economy, and the K economy informs the consumer. Those with assets, those with fewer assets or no assets, those with high incomes, those
turns.zh: ——以及在这套多资产信贷策略里，您目前低配（underweight）的又是哪些领域？那么更宽泛地说，想想这个 K 型经济（K-shaped economy），而 K 型经济影响着消费者：有资产的人、资产较少或没有资产的人、高收入的人、

turns.en: with low incomes, those with strong credit scores, those with weaker credit scores. And while we root for all consumers and all households here in America and globally, how we invest is to lean into the stronger credits and lean away from the weaker credits, particularly with respect to consumer credit.
turns.zh: ——低收入的人、信用评分（credit score）强的人、信用评分较弱的人。尽管我们为美国和全球所有消费者、所有家庭加油，但我们的投资方式是向更强的信用倾斜、远离较弱的信用，尤其是在消费信贷方面。

turns.en: So consumer credit, unsecured, that you might find in the ABS market, might be something we might lean away from, where in CNBS, a fully leased portfolio being able to buy a credit trunch, because we do all the work and we have the remains reports we have done the work
turns.zh: ——所以无担保的消费信贷，就是你可能在 ABS 市场里看到的那种，可能是我们会远离的；而在 CMBS 里，一个已经全额出租的资产组合，能够买入一个信用分层（credit tranche），是因为我们做了全部功课、拿到了兑付报告（remittance reports），我们已经对

turns.en: on every loan that backs that CNBS, we reverse engineer the transaction, and we understand how much asset coverage we have relative to the slice of risk that we're taking. If we were to be having the same conversation in, let's call it two years time from now,
turns.zh: ——支撑那笔 CMBS 的每一笔贷款都做过功课，我们会对交易进行逆向拆解（reverse engineer），也清楚相对于我们所承担的那一小片风险，我们拥有多少资产覆盖（asset coverage）。假如我们从现在起、就算两年之后吧，再来做同样的这场对话，

turns.en: what do you think that the market will have had as its biggest misconception about credit markets today? That's a big question, biggest misconception. I'd have to go with that the market's fully valued. And credit markets as credit markets, credit markets, credit spreads.
turns.zh: ——您觉得届时市场会认为，今天对信贷市场最大的误解是什么？这是个大问题——最大的误解。我大概会说，是认为市场已经被充分定价（fully valued）。而信贷市场就是信贷市场，信贷市场、信用利差（credit spreads）——

turns.en: There is so much dispersion, there is so much differentiation, there is so much opportunity, there is so much need for capital, there's excess spread everywhere we look, and overvalued securities in other places. So while the average might be fairly valued or some might claim fully valued, the dispersion
turns.zh: ——里面有太多的分化，太多的差异，太多的机会，太多的资本需求；我们放眼望去到处都是超额利差（excess spread），而在另一些地方则是被高估的证券。所以尽管平均水平也许定价合理，或者有人会说已被充分定价，但信用标的之间

turns.en: of credits and where opportunities lie, continue to allow us with the thousands and 10,000 of securities that you can select from. Again, imagine a structured credit market is 50,000 separate securities alone. And you have tens of thousands between corporate and broadly syndicate loans and emerging
turns.zh: ——的分化、以及机会所在，仍然让我们能够在成千上万、乃至数以万计的证券中进行挑选。再想想，光是结构化信贷市场就有 5 万只独立证券。而在公司债、广泛银团贷款以及新兴

turns.en: markets that you can tack on on top of that. The dispersion point is so powerful, I always think of that example of my heads in the freezer and my legs are in the oven, so on average I'm a good temperature. So on average the market might be fully priced, but you say there's a lot of dispersion out there, right?
turns.zh: ——市场之上，你还能再叠加数以万计的标的。这个“分化”的观点太有说服力了，我总会想起那个例子：我的头在冷冻室里，腿在烤箱里，所以平均下来我体温正好。也就是说，市场平均看也许已被充分定价，但您是说市面上其实有大量的分化，对吧？

turns.en: As you were talking that through, I thought it would be a good chance to talk about the software sector, because that's one area not only that's become under more scrutiny recently, but I know you've talked about how some of the, I guess, the warning signs were obvious sooner.
turns.zh: 听您这么一路讲下来，我觉得正好可以聊聊软件板块，因为那不仅是近来受到更多审视的一个领域，而且我知道您谈到过，其中一些，我猜，预警信号其实更早就已经很明显了。

turns.en: And so what do you think investors missed in the software sector and how are you thinking about that area right now in the credit markets? It's interesting to me that software, if you look in the private credit markets, or excuse me, if you look in the private markets and you look at any company with $100,000 or
turns.zh: ——那么您觉得投资者在软件板块错过了什么？如今在信贷市场里您又是如何看待这个领域的？有意思的是，软件这块，如果你看私募信贷市场——抱歉，如果你看私募市场，去看任何一家营收在 10 万美元或

turns.en: more in revenue, only 1% of the companies in this country with $100,000 more in revenue is a software company. If you look in the public equity markets around 6.5% to 7% of all public companies, not market weight, just single name weight, 6.5% to 7% are software companies.
turns.zh: ——以上的公司，这个国家里营收 10 万美元以上的公司中，只有 1% 是软件公司。而如果你看公开股票市场，所有上市公司里大约有 6.5% 到 7%——不是按市值权重，就是按单个公司数量——有 6.5% 到 7% 是软件公司。

turns.en: So it makes sense to me that the high yield market would get it right, that only 3% of all high yield is software, only 3%. But you go to the broadly syndicate loan market, 13% of those companies are software companies. Yeah. If you go to direct lending, the numbers 23%, if you go to the upper tier of direct lending,
turns.zh: ——所以在我看来，高收益市场把这一点做对了是合理的：所有高收益债里只有 3% 是软件，只有 3%。但你去看广泛银团贷款市场，其中 13% 是软件公司。是的。你去看直接贷款（direct lending），这个数字是 23%；去看直接贷款的较高层级，

turns.en: the numbers 26%, the top BDCs have 20% exposure to software. So I think it's going to be, this year is the year 2026 is the year of the awakening where people have recognized the valuation reset for software. And the valuation is, for enterprise value, it's been cut in half.
turns.zh: ——数字是 26%；顶尖的业务发展公司（BDC）对软件的敞口达到 20%。所以我认为，今年——2026 年——是“觉醒之年”，人们已经认识到软件正在经历估值重置（valuation reset）。而且就企业价值（enterprise value）而言，估值已经被腰斩。

turns.en: And so it simply can't support the level of indebtedness, because in the broadly syndicate loan market, while you have 5.2 times of leverage for your senior secured software loan. In the direct lending marketplace, those ratios are 6 times to 10 times, debt to EBITDA,
turns.zh: ——所以它根本无法支撑这样的负债水平，因为在广泛银团贷款市场里，你的优先担保（senior secured）软件贷款杠杆是 5.2 倍；而在直接贷款市场里，这些比率是 6 倍到 10 倍的债务与 EBITDA 之比（debt to EBITDA），

turns.en: with an average of around 8 times debt to EBITDA for your average software company. It can't support a terms of leverage. There's not enough free cash flow over time to support that. And it won't be, and it won't be refinanceable at 8 times, or 6 times, or even 5 times, and you go for it basis.
turns.zh: ——一般的软件公司平均大约是 8 倍债务与 EBITDA 之比。以这样的杠杆水平，它是撑不住的；随着时间推移，没有足够的自由现金流（free cash flow）来支撑。而且它没法在 8 倍、6 倍、甚至 5 倍的水平上进行再融资（refinance），按任何口径算都一样。

turns.en: And so risk management rule number one for me is portfolio diversification, not for diversity sake, but for risk sake. And so how you have more than 10 to 15% of your portfolio in any one sector is unexplainable to me. It's that simple. Number one. Number two, software is not an industry. TMT is an industry.
turns.zh: ——所以对我来说，风险管理的第一条原则是组合分散化（diversification），不是为了分散而分散，而是为了控制风险。因此，你把组合的 10% 到 15% 以上押在任何一个行业上，在我看来都是无法解释的。就这么简单。第一点。第二点，软件不是一个行业，TMT 才是一个行业。

turns.en: It's telecom, it's media, it's technology. And technology is software hardware and IT services. Software is only a small subset of the overall TMT. It may be a very important subset. And by the way, software is not going anywhere, it'll just all be AI based.
turns.zh: ——它是电信、是媒体、是科技。而科技又包括软件、硬件和 IT 服务。软件只是整个 TMT 中一个很小的子集，也许是一个非常重要的子集。顺带一提，软件不会消失，它只是会全部变成基于 AI 的。

turns.en: And so the companies that make it through will be those that can take catbacks and reinvent themselves to be AI first software companies. And the ones that won't make it through will be the others. And so I think the public companies have a fighting chance.
turns.zh: ——所以能挺过来的公司，将是那些能够投入资本开支（capex）、把自己重塑为“AI 优先”软件公司的企业；挺不过来的，就是其余那些。因此我认为，上市公司还是有一战之力的。

turns.en: And although their valuations are trading quite low, they have a fighting chance of making it through because they have great margins and lots of free cash flow. And by the way, very little debt to average debt of a public software company is 0.5 debt to EBITDA. It has less than one turn of debt.
turns.zh: ——而且尽管它们的估值交易在相当低的水平，它们仍有机会挺过来，因为它们有很高的利润率和大量自由现金流。顺带一提，它们的债务非常少：上市软件公司的平均债务为 0.5 倍债务与 EBITDA 之比，债务不到一倍杠杆。

turns.en: And so it has lots of free cash flow after debt service to make this transition. When you're a private software company that's super highly levered, you don't have that flexibility. And when you do have a default, I think it'll be punishing because when you're losing
turns.zh: ——所以在偿债之后，它还有大量自由现金流来完成这一转型。而当是一家杠杆极高的私募软件公司时，你就没有这种灵活性。而且一旦真的发生违约（default），我认为惩罚会很重，因为当你在失去

turns.en: your subscriber base, software companies don't have much recovery value when it has to go through an actual bankruptcy process, I believe. So it's going to be a challenging place to be in the next two to three years because this is the year of the valuation resect, 2026.
turns.zh: ——你的订阅用户基础的时候，我相信软件公司在真正走破产程序时的回收价值（recovery value）并不高。所以未来两到三年，这会是一个很有挑战的领域，因为 2026 年正是估值重置之年。

turns.en: And the maturity walls come in 2027, 28, and 29, the next three years. And we'll see which companies make it through a valuation and refining their debt as well as the transition with respect to their business model to being an AI first software company. It's quite unknown as we all sit here right now.
turns.zh: ——而到期墙（maturity wall）会在接下来三年、也就是 2027、2028 和 2029 年到来。我们会看到哪些公司能挺过估值、完成债务再融资，以及把商业模式转型为“AI 优先”软件公司。此刻我们坐在这里，这一切还相当未知。

turns.en: Anyone that's looking to a portfolio doesn't have that answer. It represents risk and some reward because you're getting paid coupons, but it represents risk that's unquantifiable, I believe. As you were talking there, I also was reflecting that software is also where a lot of the noise has come around private credit.
turns.zh: ——任何一个看着自己组合的人都给不出这个答案。它既代表风险、也代表一些回报，因为你在收取票息（coupon），但我认为它代表的是一种无法量化的风险。听您这么讲的时候，我也在想，软件其实也正是围绕私募信贷的很多噪音的来源。

turns.en: And so as you think about being an investor who invests in both in both public and private credit, what is real and what is not real in the news, the noise, the volatility around private credit right now? Let me define private credit to start. So private credit is direct lending, asset-based lending, and opportunistic credit strategies.
turns.zh: ——那么，作为一个既投资公开信贷、又投资私募信贷的投资者，您觉得当下围绕私募信贷的新闻、噪音、波动里，哪些是真的、哪些不是真的？让我先给私募信贷下个定义。私募信贷包括直接贷款、资产基础贷款（asset-based lending），以及机会型信贷策略（opportunistic credit）。

turns.en: So direct lending, there's all kinds of elements of direct lending. There's U.S. There's direct lending that's sponsor-based and non-sponsored-backed. There's lower-middle markets, middle markets, upper-middle markets. There's the senior loan, the mezzanine loan, or the inner trance when you put it together.
turns.zh: ——直接贷款里有各种各样的要素。有美国的直接贷款；有由私募基金支持（sponsor-based）的，也有无 sponsor 支持的；有低端中端市场（lower-middle market）、中端市场（middle market）、高端中端市场（upper-middle market）；有优先贷款（senior loan）、夹层贷款（mezzanine loan），或者当你把它们组合在一起时的内部分层（inner tranche）。

turns.en: And so there are segments of the marketplace that we lean into. We like non-cyclical businesses in the middle markets where we have covenant protection and where we're rather certain that our loss rate will be close to zero.
turns.zh: ——所以市场里有一些板块是我们倾向于加码的。我们喜欢中端市场里的非周期性业务，在这些地方我们有契约保护（covenant protection），而且我们相当确定自己的损失率（loss rate）会接近于零。

turns.en: The industry takes a much more aggressive approach in going throughout the spectrum of how they lend. And so the loss rates have been close to 1% for direct lending. Now 1% for direct lending isn't great, but it's not bad either. Because if you use eternal leverage and you're generating 11 to 12% portfolio yield,
turns.zh: ——而整个行业在放贷的整个谱系上采取的方式要激进得多。所以直接贷款的损失率一直接近 1%。对直接贷款来说，1% 说不上好，但也不算坏。因为如果你使用外部杠杆（external leverage），并产生 11% 到 12% 的组合收益率，

turns.en: then instead of 12, you earn 11. It's not bad. So the loss of just the returns for direct lending are still rather healthy. The question is based upon the legacy portfolio that dates back from 2020 to 2024 vintage deals that's heavily exposed to software, will those loss rates go up considerably?
turns.zh: ——那么你不是赚 12%，而是赚 11%，这不算坏。所以直接贷款经损失调整后的回报（loss-adjusted returns）仍然相当健康。问题在于，基于那些从 2020 到 2024 年份（vintage）、对软件敞口很重的存量组合，这些损失率会不会大幅上升？

turns.en: I believe the answer is yes, but we don't know that answer yet. We'll see in the next two to three years, those managers are under pressure. It's like the David Bowie song. Yeah. And he's got that one famous line in there and my friends screaming, let me out. Right? Yeah. And there is no out. There's no out for that.
turns.zh: ——我相信答案是肯定的，但我们现在还不知道答案。未来两到三年会见分晓，那些管理人正承受压力。这就像那首 David Bowie 的歌。是的。歌里有那么一句著名的歌词，“我的朋友们在尖叫，放我出去”。对吧？是的。可根本没有“出去”这回事，对此是没有出路的。

turns.en: And so we're going to have to see how that pick goes through the Python and how clean it is, how long it takes, and what the net results are.
turns.zh: ——所以我们得看看这个过程会怎么走、走得干不干净、要花多久，以及最终净结果如何。

turns.en: And you talked about how you need to be careful about which component of which segments of private credit you're talking about as well. Do you think this is more of a investor education component? Now that we're, it's investor education, investors here.
turns.zh: ——您还谈到，你需要小心自己说的到底是私募信贷的哪个部分、哪个板块。您觉得这在多大程度上是一个投资者教育（investor education）的问题？既然我们现在……这首先是投资者教育的问题，而这里的投资者——

turns.en: It's we're talking about retail investors. It's investor education number one. Number two, to kind of level set and put in perspective, the private credit market is around 2.1 trillion, according to JP Morgan's latest statistic. And there's around 40 billion of the retail product
turns.zh: ——我们说的是散户投资者（retail investors）。第一，这是投资者教育的问题。第二，为了把视角摆平、放到合适的背景里看：根据 JP Morgan 最新的统计，私募信贷市场大约在 2.1 万亿美元。而其中想要撤出的零售产品规模大约有 400 亿美元——

turns.en: that wants out. That's 2%. Yeah. And there's less than 20 billion that I've got now. That's far. Yes. And so there's a little bit more to accommodate. But overall, direct lending is is drawing a more money than that 2% that's left. Right. And so I believe the market's in very good shape
turns.zh: ——想要撤出的部分。那只占 2%。是的。而且现在真正赎回的还不到 200 亿美元，差得远。是的。所以还有稍微多一点需要消化。但总体而言，直接贷款吸引进来的资金，要多于那撤出的 2%。对。所以我相信市场处于非常好的状态，

turns.en: to a grow and be accommodate the redemption requests. Bruce, thank you so much. I've enjoyed every part of this conversation to learn a little bit more about you. We wanted to finish with what we call a lightning round where we basically just asked you to declare yourself as either risk on or
turns.zh: ——足以增长并消化这些赎回请求。Bruce，非常感谢您。我很享受这场对话的每一部分，也多了解了您一些。我们想以一个我们称之为“快问快答”（lightning round）的环节来收尾：基本上就是请您表明，自己究竟是“追逐风险”（risk on）还是

turns.en: risk off to the following some serious, some not so serious topics. So, so if you're willing to play the game, let's go. Great. In chess, would you be willing to start with a king's gambit? I'm a queen and I'm always risk on. Always risk on. If your opponent does,
turns.zh: ——“规避风险”（risk off），针对下面这些话题，有的严肃、有的不那么严肃。那么，如果您愿意玩这个游戏，我们开始吧。好。在国际象棋里，您愿意以“王翼弃兵”（King’s Gambit）开局吗？我选“后”（queen），而且我永远都是 risk on。永远 risk on。如果您的对手这么走，

turns.en: do you accept or decline? Except. Except. I never quit. It feels like risk on.
turns.zh: ——您是接受还是拒绝？接受，接受，我从不退缩。这听起来像是 risk on。

turns.en: Will there be a recession in the next 12 months? No. No. So that risk is risk on. Risk on absolutely. Risk on absolutely. Oh, you want to risk on a risk offence or got it? Exactly. Risk on. No recession. Exactly. When we spoke earlier, you talked about when you go to
turns.zh: ——未来 12 个月会出现经济衰退（recession）吗？不会，不会。那这是 risk off 吗？绝对是 risk on，绝对是 risk on。哦，你是在一个本该 risk off 的话题上选了 risk on，明白了？正是，risk on——没有衰退，没错。

turns.en: Australia, you like to visit Manly Beach. Lovely stunning beach. There's been a shock alert there in the last week. Are you still going swimming? I start to rocks and go down to the key, take the boat across to Manly and go for a swim. And I would never miss it. Shock or no shock.
turns.zh: ——我们之前聊的时候，您提到去澳大利亚时喜欢到 Manly Beach 走走，那是个美得惊人的海滩。过去一周那里发布了鲨鱼警报（shark alert）。您还会去游泳吗？我会从 The Rocks 出发，走到环形码头（Circular Quay），坐船过海到 Manly，然后去游个泳。我绝不会错过，有没有鲨鱼警报都一样。

turns.en: I would never miss it. But when there are shock warnings, you make sure that like there's a few people beyond where you are. And so it's like kind of like that story of outrunning the bear. Yep. You're not getting all this. Exactly. And so I'm always way in from, you know,
turns.zh: ——我绝不会错过。但当有鲨鱼警报时，你会确保自己所在位置往外还有几个人。所以就有点像那个“跑赢熊”的故事。对。反正落后的不会是你。没错。所以只要有一丝担心，我永远都会离人群那条线远远的，你知道——

turns.en: where the line of people are. If there's any concern about that whatsoever. All right. I'm calling that risk on. I'm calling that risk off. Risk off. Okay. I mean, you're in, but not more scoff. Okay. You're conditional. Yes. Valuation sensitive. The next one. So as a tennis player, are you going for it on a second serve?
turns.zh: ——离人群所在的那条线远远的，只要对此有任何一丁点担心。好吧。这个我算 risk on。我算 risk off。risk off。好吧。我的意思是，你会下水，但不会更冒进。好。你是有条件的。是的，对估值敏感。下一个。那么作为一名网球选手，你在二发（second serve）时会全力搏杀吗？

turns.en: No. I'm not on the second serve. Second service is my safety serve. I'm making sure I get it in. But I'm going to play that next point very aggressively. Got it. That feels like risk off to me. Risk off. Risk off. Yeah. You've written about this by the end of 2027, we won't have
turns.zh: ——不会，二发我不会搏杀。二发是我的安全发球，我要确保发进去。但接下来那一分我会打得非常激进。明白了。这在我看来像是 risk off。risk off，risk off。是的。

turns.en: dot plots from the Fed anymore. Yeah. Well, you know, very interesting that our new Fed chair, Kevin Warrz, was the only dot not to have voted. And so he doesn't want the level of transparency that, you know, Bernanke really brought to the forefront in 2012 when he invented dots,
turns.zh: ——您写过，到 2027 年底，我们将不再有来自美联储（Fed）的点阵图（dot plot）。是的。嗯，你知道，很有意思的是，我们新任的美联储主席 Kevin Warsh 是唯一一个没有参与投票的点。所以他并不想要那种程度的透明度——你知道，是 Bernanke 在 2012 年发明点阵图时把这种透明度真正推到台前的，

turns.en: Bernanke in 2012. And so here we are 14 years later. And I do believe, although he hasn't said that, he wants to do it with the dots, because it's too fixed on what's going to happen in the future. And he wants to have that flexibility and not telegraph that and have to defend that or have
turns.zh: ——Bernanke 在 2012 年。所以 14 年后的今天到了这里。我确实相信，尽管他没有明说，但他想对点阵图下手（取消它），因为它把未来会发生什么固定得太死。他想拥有那种灵活性，不去提前透露、不必去为之辩护，也不必

turns.en: to move to that motion because he's told markets that. Okay. So I call that risk on, because it's going to bring more volatility on transparency. Got it. Uh, you've talked a lot about AI today. And so AI ultimately is going to be risk on a risk off for employment growth.
turns.zh: ——不必被迫转向那个方向，因为他已经这样告诉过市场了。好。那我把这个算作 risk on，因为它会带来更多波动、更少透明度。明白了。嗯，您今天谈了很多 AI。那么归根结底，AI 对就业增长来说会是 risk on 还是 risk off？

turns.en: AI is risk on by its very nature, because it's transformative. It needs a lot of capital.
turns.zh: ——AI 本质上就是 risk on，因为它是变革性的。它需要大量资本。

turns.en: Employment. I'm not an employment bearer based upon AI. I will reassess that in next five to seven years, but next five years, it creates more jobs, not eliminates more jobs. Thank you so much for your time. My pleasure. Great to be with you. You too.
turns.zh: ——就业方面，我并不因为 AI 而对就业持悲观（bear）态度。未来五到七年我会重新评估，但就接下来五年而言，它创造的岗位多于它消灭的岗位。非常感谢您抽出时间。我很荣幸。很高兴与您交流。您也是。

turns.en: Well, mate, that's our show for today. Remember, in your personal life and your investing life, keep breaking boundaries.
turns.zh: ——好了，伙计，我们今天的节目就到这里。记住，在你的个人生活和投资生活中，都要不断突破边界（keep breaking boundaries）。
